BALANCED TWO-GENERATOR p-GROUPS OF DEFICIENCY ZERO
         AND UNBOUNDED NILPOTENCY CLASS

                                          GROUPTHEORY50


        Abstract. For every prime p > 3 we construct an explicit family of finite two-
        generator p-groups of deficiency zero whose nilpotency classes tend to infinity. The
        construction gives, for every n ≥ 1, a group of order p2n+1 and class n + 1. This gives
        an affirmative answer to Problem 17.113 of the Kourovka Notebook.




                                         1. Introduction
  The deficiency of a finite presentation
                                      ⟨x1 , . . . , xd | r1 , . . . , rs ⟩
is d−s, and the deficiency of a finitely presented group is the supremum of the deficiencies
of its finite presentations. A presentation with the same number of generators and relators
is usually called balanced. Balanced presentations of finite p-groups are constrained
enough to be useful in topology and combinatorial group theory, but flexible enough to
support groups of substantial nilpotency class.
   Problem 17.113 of the Kourovka Notebook, proposed by J. Wiegold in the 17th
issue, asks whether, for a fixed prime p > 3, there are two-generator finite p-groups of
deficiency zero with arbitrarily high nilpotency class [1]. We give a uniform metacyclic
construction.

                                             2. The family
  Fix a prime p > 3 and an integer n ≥ 1. Define
                                  D                                     n        n
                                                                                     E
                           Gn = a, b b−1 ab = a1+p ,                   bp = ap           .
We use the commutator convention [x, y] = x−1 y −1 xy.
Theorem 2.1. For every n ≥ 1, the group Gn is a finite two-generator p-group of order
p2n+1 , nilpotency class n + 1, and deficiency zero.
                                         n           n
Proof. Conjugating the relation bp = ap by b gives
                                                 n           n
                                             bp = ap (1+p) .
                                                                 n+1                         n+1
Comparison with the defining relation yields ap = 1, and then also bp = 1. Using
 −1     1+p                          i j              pn   p n
b ab = a , every word collects to a b . The relation b = a allows us to choose
                                 0 ≤ i < pn+1 ,                  0 ≤ j < pn ,
so |Gn | ≤ p2n+1 .
   For the reverse inequality, put q = 1 + p and let
                       An = ⟨α⟩ =∼ C n+1 ,     Bn = ⟨β⟩ ∼
                                                        = C n+1 .
                                             p                                  p

Let Bn act on An by αβ = αq . The standard lifting-the-exponent calculation gives
                                              k
                                      vp (q p − 1) = k + 1,
so this automorphism has order pn . In Sn = An ⋊ Bn the element
                                                      n     n
                                          z = β p α−p
is central of order p. Moreover ⟨z⟩ meets both An and Bn trivially. Hence
                                     Hn = Sn /⟨z⟩
has order p 2n+1 . The images of α and β satisfy the defining relations of G
                                                                    n , so there is
                                                                    ∼
an epimorphism Gn ↠ Hn . The upper bound already obtained forces Gn = Hn .
  The first defining relation gives
                                              [a, b] = ap ,
and therefore, for k ≥ 0,
                                              k            k+1
                                        [ap , b] = ap            .
It follows inductively that
                                          r−1
                             γr (Gn ) = ⟨ap       ⟩       (2 ≤ r ≤ n + 2).
Thus γn+1 (Gn ) ̸= 1 and γn+2 (Gn ) = 1, so the class is n + 1.
   The displayed presentation has two generators and two relators, hence def(Gn ) ≥ 0.
On the other hand, if a finite group has a presentation with d generators and s relators,
abelianization and tensoring the relation matrix with Q show that s ≥ d; thus every
finite group has deficiency at most zero. Consequently def(Gn ) = 0.                  □
Corollary 2.2. By Theorem 2.1, for every prime p > 3 there exist two-generator finite
p-groups of deficiency zero and arbitrarily large nilpotency class.

                                    3. Further remarks
   The groups Gn are metacyclic central quotients of semidirect products of two cyclic
p-groups. In particular, the growth of nilpotency class does not require a growing number
of generators or relators. The same presentation also gives a concrete family suitable for
computational experiments with balanced finite presentations.
   The restriction p > 3 is the one appearing in the Kourovka problem. The construction
itself uses only the familiar p-adic behavior of 1 + p for odd p; we have not attempted
here to optimize the small-prime range.
